zero_cer_audit.notes: Filtered to realized_cer == 0 and label == 'drift' (a clean input the ensemble nonetheless called drift on). Precedence: critical_substitution > formatting > paraphrase > overgenerative > other -- each row is assigned the first cause it matches, not summed across causes. critical_substitution = any of ['crit_negation_flip', 'crit_numeral_change', 'crit_recipient_change', 'crit_urgency_change', 'crit_actionable_omission'] is True. formatting = output_message equals intended_text after lowercasing, punctuation removal, and whitespace collapse. paraphrase = cos_mpnet and cos_minilm both >= nli_metric.COS_HI (currently 0.75) and bidirectional entailment ('entail' both directions) on at least one of the two NLI models (deberta or roberta), reached only when no crit_* flag is set. overgenerative = output_message at least 1.5x intended_text's character length, reached only when none of the above matched. other = residual. Examples are capped at 10 message_id(s) per cause.

matched_compare.notes: engine=conditional_logit (statsmodels.discrete.conditional_models.ConditionalLogit, endog=drift, exog=[critical + char_len + n_errors + corrupted_negation + corrupted_numeral + realized_cer], groups=pair_id). Conditioning is on the matched pair (pair_id, the Task-1.3 CRIT-CTRL match): every pair's group-specific intercept is differenced out of the conditional likelihood, so any confounder constant within a matched pair is controlled for without being named. coef['critical'] is the adjusted CRIT-vs-CTRL contrast; the other five entries are the adjusters' own coefficients. 63888 of 91700 input pairs dropped for having no within-group outcome variance (fully concordant -- same drift/non-drift outcome on every row in that pair, contributing nothing to a conditional likelihood; standard for conditional logistic regression, not a bug). Fit warnings: Dropped 63888 groups and 127776 observations for having no within-group variance. converged=True (fit raised no exception and every reported est/se is finite; ConditionalLogit's own .fit() does not expose the underlying optimizer's convergence flag on its returned result, see module docstring).
matched_compare._strata: pair_id x cer_target x replicate_idx x model (matched pair at identical corruption cell)
matched_compare._note: Coarse message-pair-level conditioning did not converge on the full cohort (huge strata); finer identical-corruption strata is the classic discordant-matched-pair conditional logistic and converges.

risk_difference.notes: estimand=risk_difference RD = P(drift|CRIT) - P(drift|CTRL) on the matched CRIT-vs-CTRL design (the absolute-scale companion to matched_drift's odds-ratio contrast). CI is a pair-clustered percentile bootstrap (1000 of 1000 replicates finite): whole matched pairs (pair_id) are resampled with replacement, preserving within-pair correlation across the many attempt-level rows a pair spans (models x CER targets x replicates). additional_drifts_per_1000 = RD*1000 (a pure rescale of RD and its CI). n_pairs=131, n_crit=91700, n_ctrl=91700, seed=0.

risk_difference_by_cer.notes: criticality-by-CER interaction on the absolute scale: CRIT-vs-CTRL risk difference within each cer_target level, each with its own pair-clustered percentile-bootstrap 95% CI. Reported as stratum-specific RDs (interaction_form=stratified), not a critical x cer product term, because the coarse pair-level conditional logit does not converge on the full cohort (see module docstring / digest _note); the stratified RD shows whether the absolute gap changes with corruption without optimizer fragility. Each stratum uses a distinct deterministic bootstrap stream (seed+i, base seed=0); 1000 replicates per stratum.

highlight_drift_vs_degraded_realized_cer.note: PRIMARY reviewer-requested contrast: does realized corruption push the model toward a fluent-but-wrong drift OVER an obviously-degraded output? OR > 1 means rising realized_cer favors drift over degraded.

confidently_wrong_rate.notes: confidence scale detected as 0-100 from df['confidence'].max() on 3880685 non-NaN row(s); conf_threshold=0.9 rescaled to effective_threshold=90.0 for comparison (>= is inclusive). 7315 NaN-confidence row(s) excluded from every denominator below. frac_drift_at_high_confidence = P(confidence >= threshold | label == 'drift'). confidently_wrong_rate = P(label != 'faithful' | confidence >= threshold). Report per-model, not just pooled -- confidence scales differ across models.

missing_confidence_audit.notes: 7315 of 3888000 row(s) have NaN confidence, tabulated across 16 model(s) x 5 cer_target level(s). Cells with zero missing rows are included explicitly.

predicted_drift_grid.notes: engine=statsmodels.api.Logit (label=='drift' ~ 1 + realized_cer), cov_type='cluster', cov_kwds={'groups': message_id}. Deliberately univariate (realized_cer only, no covariates or random effects) for a single quotable number per CER grid point; see idrift.analysis.mixed_models for the covariate-adjusted models. `seed` is accepted for interface consistency but unused -- this fit's Newton-Raphson MLE is already deterministic.

dependence_sensitivity.description: Alternative estimators of the realized_cer -> drift log-odds slope under different dependence assumptions across 16 models. All estimators fit realized_cer ONLY (plus intercept) for mutual comparability.

reference_slopes.note: The 4.77 headline is the ADJUSTED message-clustered logit slope (adjusts n_errors, char_len, corrupted_negation, corrupted_numeral, C(family)) from this run's mixed_model.drift.coefficients.realized_cer. The dependence estimators here are UNIVARIATE, so their natural reference is the univariate message-clustered anchor (8.12, from confidence_analysis.predicted_drift_grid). That gap is ADJUSTMENT, not dependence; this digest's question is only about dependence.

per_model_pooled_dl.label: Per-model message-clustered cluster-robust logit (drift ~ realized_cer), pooled across models by DerSimonian-Laird random-effects meta-analysis (preferred model-level estimator; 7 models is too few for a model-clustered SE)

gee.label: GEE population-averaged logit (drift ~ realized_cer; Binomial family, independence fallback working correlation, groups=message_id, robust sandwich SE)
gee.notes: FALLBACK: exchangeable working correlation returned an implausible or degenerate fit (non-finite parameters, a log-odds slope beyond 50, or a collapsed standard error), in some runs while reporting convergence on this cohort (large ~700-row message clusters with strong within-message drift correlation); reverted to an independence working correlation with the same robust sandwich SE, which yields a consistent slope and a valid cluster-robust SE regardless of the true correlation.

bootstrap_message.label: Nonparametric cluster bootstrap of drift ~ realized_cer, resampling message-level clusters (2299) with replacement, 500 resamples

bootstrap_model.label: Nonparametric cluster bootstrap of drift ~ realized_cer, resampling model-level clusters (16) with replacement, 500 resamples

conclusion.summary: The realized_cer log-odds slope is STABLE across dependence assumptions: all four estimators lie in 8.12-8.64 (spread 0.51, 6.3% max deviation from the univariate anchor 8.12). The preferred model-level estimator is the DerSimonian-Laird per-model pool (16 models; a model-clustered SE is not used because the model count is too small for that purpose); it shows between-model heterogeneity (tau^2=4.77, I^2=100%) but every model's slope is positive (range 4.1-10.8). The model-level cluster bootstrap is reported honestly as UNSTABLE (16 clusters: much wider CI than the message-level bootstrap). The exchangeable GEE diverged on this cohort and fell back to an independence working correlation (see its notes).
